note: Satanikota (Kurnool) megalithic and Stone Age excavation; 'ohind' is a false match.

author: R. S. Bisht, Mid-Eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Sarai mound temple complex at the Nalanda ruins (Nalanda district)
evidence: 1979-80: outer boundary wall of the temple complex in three phases, two brick votive stupas, tile drain, residential rooms outside the wall; terracotta sealings with the legend read \"Nalokasha\"; two corner shrines suggest a panchayatana temple
quote: resumed excavation at Sarai mound with a view to expose the structures in full … Important antiquities recovered include terracotta sealings with the legend Nalokasha and balls and stone sculptures. It may be presumed that the main shrine was a panchayatana type of temple
note: Continues passage 377 (1978-79). Sarai mound lies at Mizutani's Nalanda ruins (09.03.01, agreed; asr Cunningham). The sealing legend as printed ('Nalokasha') is unexplained and does not clearly name Nalanda; no reference to Xuanzang.
Jamnagar explorations and Dwarka excavation; 'Und' is a river name, false match.
Exploration in Amaravati district (Maharashtra), not the Amaravati stupa; Salbardi caves.

author: Epigraphy Branch, ASI
asr_identification: Sirpur (Raipur district), seat of the issuing king
evidence: Three copper plates of Sudevaraja found at Mahasamund, box-headed Brahmi dated by the editor to the 5th century, issued from Sirpura in his third regnal year
quote: COPPER-PLATES OF SUDEVARAJA, MAHASAMUND, DISTRICT RAIPUR … written in box-headed Brahmi script of the fifth century A.D. The charter issued from Sirpura, by the king Sudevaraja
note: No reference to Xuanzang. Shows Sripura as a royal seat already under Sudevaraja (Sarabhapuriya), before the Somavamsi kings of the Mallar plates; supports Mizutani's Sirpur capital for Kosala (10.12, disputed; Cunningham 1871 Chanda). The Ajanta Cave 6 painted inscription in the same section is not a location.
Epigraphy: Brindaban brick inscription, Govindnagar Huvishka Amitabha image (Mathura); no Xiyu ji location argued.
Numismatics (Kholapur, District Amaravati, Maharashtra); false match.
Museums (Mathura, Nalanda, Sarnath accessions).
Preservation (Kesaria, Nalanda Sarai mound, Jivakamravana and Rajgir hills, Kumrahar); no location argued.
Preservation in Tamil Nadu; 'Rajgiri fort, Gingee' is a false match for Rajgir.
Chemical cleaning of metal objects from the Mathura excavation.
Gardens at Kusinagar (Nirvana stupa, Ramabhar), Sahet-Mahet ('ancient Sravasti', Jetavana) and Sarnath; maintenance only.
Plate captions (Mathura museum images).

author: I. K. Sarma, Excavation Branch (I), ASI
asr_identification: Peddavegi (West Godavari) = Vengipura, capital of Andhra
evidence: 1985-86 Dhanam-Dibba mound N of the village: free-standing brick stupa on a 12.90 m square platform, Phase IA (4th-5th c., Salankayana; Aparasaila pillar record of 1927); Phase IB (Vishnukundin, end 5th-7th c.) the stupa neglected and Brahmanical temples of red sandstone built, Vishnukundin and Eastern Chalukya coins; Kalabhairava images at the city boundary beyond the ruined fortification
quote: has undertaken the excavation at the ancient historical city of Vengipura, now a sprawling village called Peddavegi … It may be recalled that the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang (AD 620-644) made a mention of a Stupa caused by Asoka-Maurya at Ping-Ki-Pu-lo i.e. Vengipura … The stupa was no more found to be important and the occupants built Brahmanical temples
note: Second season after passage 440 (1984-85), before 456-457 (1986-87). Confirms Mizutani's Vengi at Peddavegi (10.13, agreed; Cunningham 1871 Elgandel). The excavator connects Xuanzang's Asoka stupa with Dhanam-Dibba only by implication; the stupa's eclipse by temples in Phase IB fits Xuanzang's few monks and many deva temples in Andhra. Nothing found names Vengi.

author: Ajit Kumar Prasad under Sita Ram Roy and Naseem Akhtar, Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Bihar
name_in_asr: Taradih mound, SW of the Mahabodhi temple, Bodh-Gaya
evidence: 1985-86: seven periods from Neolithic; Period VI Gupta and late Gupta brick structures, votive stupas, Buddha images, sealings; Period VII Pala monastery with stone pillar bases, verandah and three rooms, seals, sealings, Buddha, Avalokitesvara and Tara
quote: resumed excavations at Taradih mound, located to the south-west of Mahabodhi temple at Bodh-Gaya … Period VI was marked by the appearance of Gupta and late Gupta antiquities along with the structural remains of burnt bricks
note: As passages 398, 427, 458: monastic remains in Mizutani's Bodh Gaya precinct (08.06.01); no Xiyu ji structure identified and Xuanzang not named.

author: Centre of Central Asian Studies, Kashmir University
evidence: Exploration of the Mughal route Chingas-Thana Mandi: Kushan red ware at Kheora 1.5 km above Rajouri; coins of Jayapida-Vinayaditya and Harsha of Kashmir reported from Panjnara; temple ruins at Panjnara of Kashmiri plan
quote: Hiuen Tstang in seventh century AD who returned to the plains through this area mentions that the hill state of Rajapuri (modern Rajouri) and Parnotsa (modern Poonch), were not independent but were subjected to Kashmir. Coins of Jayapida-Vinayaditya and of Harsha were reported to have been found at Panjnara substantiating thereby Kashmir's suzerainty
note: Agrees with Mizutani (03.08 Rajaori, 03.07 Punch, both agreed). The Kashmir coins are of the 8th and 11th centuries, so they bear on Kashmiri control generally, not on Xuanzang's time.

author: G. C. Chauley, Bhubaneswar Circle, ASI
evidence: 1985-86: stupa 15 m in diameter at base, rubble core veneered with dressed sandstone, paved pradakshinapatha 3 m wide; three khondalite relic caskets (two with steatite, silver and gold caskets enclosing bone relics), the first relic caskets reported in Orissa
quote: Another epoch making discovery is the relic caskets (pl. XIXA) not reported from any other site in Orissa … The gold caskets contain the relics in the shape of small piece of bone (pl. XIXB) … Since it contains relics of Buddha, it might be the same stupa noticed by Hiuen-Tsang.
note: Tentative; the report does not say which of Xuanzang's Odra stupas is meant, most likely the light-emitting stone stupa of Puspagiri (10.09.02). Differs from Mizutani's Khandagiri (agreed; Cunningham Udayagiri-Khandagiri). Lalitgiri lies N of the Mahanadi, inside Odra on Chakravarti's boundary (10.09). Later Lalitgiri seasons (passages 459, 512) do not repeat the claim.
Sanghol (Ludhiana) Kushan finds and ink inscription; Taxila named only as an ivory-comb parallel.
Hulaskhera (Lucknow) excavation and Mathura PGW exploration; no Xiyu ji place.
Jammu and Karnataka finds; Katra near Riasi is a false match.
Kushana railing pillars at Palikheda (Mathura) and other UP/West Bengal finds; no location argued.
Palaeobotany (Ahichchhatra charcoal identifications).
Museums (Sarnath gallery reorganised).
Preservation (Madan Mohan temple, Vrindaban).
Preservation (Nalanda, Old Rajgriha, Kolhua stupa, Kushinagar).
Archaeological chemistry (Mathura sandstone conservation).
Gardens (Sarnath) and publications (Nalanda guide).
